Subject: Request for SOC 2 / SIG evidence — Dedicated & Private separation

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the rapid demo yesterday. Pinnacle (our auditor) has started the initial evidence intake for our upcoming SOC 2 and SIG review. They asked us for a concise package that demonstrates logical and network separation between Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, plus controls around the control plane and KMS boundaries.

Can you provide the following by COB 2026-10-15?
- Annotated network diagram showing Dedicated vs Private demarcation (data/control plane labels)
- Microsegmentation matrix (service -> allowed listeners, ports, direction)
- Control plane egress/ingress matrix (what talks to what, managed vs customer-controlled)
- KMS/HSM boundary statement (how CMKs are protected, who can export keys)
- Evidence index (hashes/checksums for files, test artifacts)

Also let us know if you can provide any sample firewall/iptables rules or sanitized pcap excerpts showing isolation testing. Pinnacle will need an owner contact to schedule a 30 minute technical walkthrough next week.

If we can get the packet by next Thursday that keeps us on schedule.

Thanks,
Samir Khan

Thanks for the fast turnaround — we reviewed the index and the microseg matrix. A couple of clarifying asks from Pinnacle before they accept the pack:

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the specific asks; below are concise answers and the next action items. I've also uploaded the redacted artifacts to the shared Drive and added a checksum index. Link and IDs are in the evidence index.

Answers: 1) DNS & metadata flows
- Dedicated and Private deployments do not share tenant DNS resolvers. Each tenancy attaches to an isolated resolver set (logical SVC endpoints in our VPC) that is unreachable from other tenant VPCs except via tightly controlled and logged bridge interfaces used only for customer-approved interconnects.
- Metadata endpoints (internal metadata service) are local to each deployment plane and are behind a service proxy that enforces per-tenant ACLs. We included a small diagram inset in the annotated network PDF illustrating the metadata proxy flow.

2) KMS export policy / HSM details
- We operate AWS KMS for hosted and Dedicated-managed keys using AWS CloudHSM-backed keys for workloads that require HSM. We do not export plaintext key material under any contracted plan. Customer-managed CMKs are supported inside their VPCs in Private deployments — export of key material is prohibited by policy and by HSM constraints.
- HSM vendor: AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated modules). A signed statement and vendor cert are included in kms_boundary_attestation.txt.

3) Testing artifacts
- Uploaded: redacted_isolation_pcap_20261014_redacted.pcap (pcap stub) and the filter script isolate_redact.sh (bash) used to remove IPs and customer identifiers.
- iptables sample: example_iptables_snippets.txt with comments on where rules are applied (host vs sidecar).
- Logs: acceptance_test_connectivity.log (sanitized) showing test vectors and timestamps.

Runbook / ticket: JIRA-RUNBOOK-2147 contains our key rotation and compromise playbook; I put a short export PDF in the Drive.

Next steps / owners:
- Kimberly to schedule technical walkthrough with Pinnacle & BlueRiver (action: Kimberly)
- Karthik will produce a one-page control narrative mapping SIG items to our artifacts (action: Karthik)
- Soojin will produce a short attestation memo for tenant fencing and microseg controls (action: Soojin)

We aim to have the sanitized pcap and iptables examples in the Drive by 2026-10-14 (we shipped the initial index and diagrams today). If Pinnacle wants live access for a remote screen-share to see the topology in the console, we can provision a 15-minute session with redwood infra.
